summary: Guyana lets CARICOM nationals live and travel freely under Caribbean Community arrangements and admits a broad list of Commonwealth, European and American passports visa-free, for up to 90 days where the Foreign Ministry states a period; everyone else needs a visa arranged in advance through a Guyanese mission.

fee.notes: Payable on arrival for a stay of one month (Foreign Ministry advisory). Extensions are handled by Immigration Support Services, which grants at most two, of three months each, for a GYD 5,125 processing fee; the advisory's older terms were one month and USD 25 per extension. The Foreign Ministry's advisory offers this route to visa nationals who are unable to apply at a Guyanese mission or consulate, and Immigration Support Services takes the application online before you travel, with a mandatory letter requesting a visa on arrival.

source.name: Immigration Support Services, Ministry of Home Affairs — visitor visa application

conflict.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Guyana — Advisory on visas on arrival and visa fees
conflict.states: at most two extensions of one month each, USD 25 per extension

fee.notes: The Foreign Ministry's advisory on visas issued on arrival prices the business visa at USD 140 for five years, with each five-year renewal costing another USD 140; no official source publishes a separate fee for a business visa issued by a mission. The company and its contact in Guyana must be notified to the Ministry of Home Affairs before you travel.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Guyana — Advisory on visas on arrival and visa fees

fee.notes: Processing fee for an extension of stay of three months, payable in cash or by manager's cheque to the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; GYD 28,700 if the extension granted exceeds three months. Apply to Immigration Support Services with a letter to its Head requesting the extension and evidence of funds for the longer stay. At most two extensions are granted.

source.name: Immigration Support Services, Ministry of Home Affairs of Guyana — Visitor Visa Extension

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 4 hours through the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Guyana is itself on WHO's list of countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

currencyLimits.text: Travelers carrying more than USD 10,000 in foreign currency (or the equivalent in another currency) into or out of Guyana must complete a Declaration of International Transportation of Currency, available at the international airports and the Lethem and Suriname ferry crossings. Failing to declare, or declaring falsely, is an offence punishable by a fine, up to six months' imprisonment and forfeiture of the undeclared cash.

notes: Canada's travel advice says importing or exporting restricted items, including firearms and ammunition, without the proper permits may result in heavy fines and prison sentences.
The UK government's travel advice says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Guyana, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says only major hotels accept credit cards, that there are a few ATMs that accept international bank cards, and that the US dollar is widely accepted. It advises carrying enough cash for anticipated expenses and exchanging foreign currency only at banks, hotels and established exchange bureaus (cambios).

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are significant and police capacity is low. Muggings and attacks, sometimes with knives or firearms, happen in daylight but more often at night and can target tourists who show signs of wealth; reported hotspots in Georgetown include Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and the Botanical Gardens. Gangs have followed cars from Cheddi Jagan International Airport, so drive with doors locked and use a taxi booked by your hotel or a licensed operator.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says Guyana has two rainy seasons, from May to July and from November to January, but that flooding occurs year round and can hamper overland travel, particularly in coastal areas. The months shown are those outside the two rainy seasons; no official source we could read recommends a time to visit.

tips.text: Vehicles drive on the left in Guyana. Canada's travel advice says road conditions and road safety are poor throughout the country, roads are poorly lit, and roaming livestock are a hazard; it advises avoiding driving at night.

Canada's travel advice says to carry enough cash for your anticipated expenses, to exchange foreign currency only at banks, hotels and established exchange bureaus (cambios), and that only major hotels accept credit cards. The UK government's travel advice says to go inside the exchange office or shop rather than change money on the street.

The UK government's travel advice says visitors can normally stay for 30 days. Extensions are granted by Immigration Support Services for three months at a time, at most two. Overstaying can lead to arrest, a one-year prison sentence, a fine of up to 50,000 Guyana dollars and deportation at your own expense. Canada's travel advice says to make sure your passport is stamped on arrival.
A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission, and WHO lists Guyana itself among the countries with that risk.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guyana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. CARICOM nationals are granted a definite entry of six months. About 40 other nationalities are visa-exempt on ordinary passports, among them the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Japan, most of western Europe, and several Latin American states — 90 days for some, such as Albania, Brazil and Peru, and 30 days for others, such as South Korea, Singapore and South Africa; for the United States, Canada, Japan and most of western Europe the list states no period, and the UK government says British visitors can normally stay 30 days. Several EU countries, including Germany and Poland, are not on the list. Everyone else needs a visitor's visa arranged before travel through a Guyanese embassy or high commission.

faq.question: How does CARICOM free movement work in Guyana?
faq.answer: Guyana is a founding member of the Caribbean Community, and under a CARICOM Heads of Government decision that Guyana has implemented, nationals of other member states are granted a definite entry of six months. Skilled nationals with a CARICOM Skills Certificate can also live and work in Guyana.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Guyana?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from, or have spent more than 4 hours transiting through the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — then a certificate is required from age 1. WHO lists Guyana itself among the countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Guyana?
faq.answer: Only as an exception. The Foreign Ministry's advisory says visas will be issued on arrival to visa nationals who are unable to apply at a Guyanese mission or consulate, and Immigration Support Services takes these applications online before travel, with a mandatory letter requesting a visa on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Guyana?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply to Immigration Support Services (Ministry of Home Affairs) with a letter requesting the extension and evidence of funds for the longer stay. Each extension is for three months and at most two are granted; the processing fee is GYD 5,125 (GYD 28,700 if an extension of more than three months is granted).

faq.question: Is Guyana safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says attacks and muggings, sometimes with knives or firearms, occur in broad daylight but are more common at night, and names Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and Sophia in Georgetown among the areas affected; it recommends taxis from reputable companies booked in advance. Canada's travel advice says travel to the interior is not safe because of low police presence, and the FCDO says medical facilities are very limited, even in Georgetown.
